thoughts.text: Nothing is worth more than this day.
The quieter you become, the more you can hear.
Very little is needed to make a happy life.
Loss is nothing else but change, and change is nature's delight.
Look deep into nature, and then you will understand everything better.
It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
The present moment is filled with joy and happiness. If you are attentive, you will see it.
Adopt the pace of nature: her secret is patience.
We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
Walk as if you are kissing the Earth with your feet.
Wherever you are, be all there.

facts.text: The first computer bug was a real moth, found in a relay of the Harvard Mark II in 1947 and taped into the logbook.
The first message sent over ARPANET, in 1969, was meant to be LOGIN. The system crashed after the L and the O.
Ray Tomlinson chose the @ sign for email addresses in 1971, because it appeared in no one's name.
The first webcam watched a coffee pot at Cambridge University, so people could see if it was empty before walking over.
The first website went online at CERN in 1991. It has been restored and is still there, at info.cern.ch.
The first .com domain ever registered was symbolics.com, in 1985.
Bluetooth is named after Harald Bluetooth, a tenth-century king who united Denmark and Norway.
Google's search engine started life under the name BackRub.
The first computer mouse, built by Doug Engelbart's team in the 1960s, had a wooden shell.
The Python programming language is named after Monty Python, not the snake.
Junk email is called spam after a Monty Python sketch in which the word drowns out everything else.
The Apollo Guidance Computer that flew to the Moon had about 4 KB of working memory.
The original iPhone launched in 2007 without an App Store. The store opened a year later.
The word robot comes from Karel Capek's 1920 play R.U.R., from a Czech word for forced labour.
Pac-Man was called Puck Man in Japan. The name was changed for the arcades abroad.
Mario's first appearance was in Donkey Kong in 1981, where he was known as Jumpman.
Tetris was written by Alexey Pajitnov in Moscow in 1984, on a Soviet computer.
Nintendo was founded in 1889. It made playing cards.
The PlayStation began as a CD add-on that Sony was building for the Super Nintendo.
Space Invaders speeds up as you shoot the aliens because the hardware could move fewer of them faster. The designer kept it.
The first Pong machine stopped working in a bar in 1972. The coin box had overflowed.
Minecraft is the best-selling video game of all time.
The Konami Code, up up down down left right left right B A, was added by a developer who found Gradius too hard.
One of the first hidden Easter eggs in a game was Warren Robinett's secret credit in Adventure for the Atari 2600.
A toy whistle from a cereal box played 2600 Hz, the tone that controlled AT&T's long-distance lines. Phone phreaks used it to make free calls.
Hacker first meant a clever tinkerer, at MIT's Tech Model Railroad Club in the 1950s and 60s.
Creeper, in 1971, is thought of as the first computer worm. Its message: I'M THE CREEPER: CATCH ME IF YOU CAN.
The Morris Worm of 1988 slowed or stopped about a tenth of the computers on the early internet.
Brain, the first virus for IBM PCs, was written in 1986 by two brothers in Pakistan. It carried their names and address.
Leet, written 1337, comes from elite: the way early hackers spelled their status.
123456 and password are still among the most common passwords in the world.
Alan Turing's electromechanical bombes at Bletchley Park helped break the German Enigma codes.
